name: Colorado AI Act
description: SB 24-205, Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence. Imposes duties on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to prevent algorithmic discrimination in consequential decisions.

regulation.penalties: Violations constitute unfair trade practices under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act.
regulation.covered_entities: Developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems doing business in Colorado.
regulation.risk_classification: High-risk AI systems in consequential decisions (employment, lending, housing, healthcare, education, insurance, legal, government services).
regulation.applicability_notes: Effective date delayed from February 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026 by SB 25B-004 (August 2025 special session). Verify current status against the official source; amendment activity has been ongoing.

events.summary: SB 24-205 introduced in the Colorado General Assembly.
Passed by the Colorado General Assembly.
Signed by Governor Polis — first comprehensive US state AI law.
SB 25B-004 (special session) delayed the effective date from February 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026.

name: EU AI Act
description: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — the world's first comprehensive horizontal AI regulation. Risk-based framework: prohibited practices, high-risk system obligations, GPAI model duties, transparency requirements.

regulation.enforcement_authority: National market surveillance authorities; European AI Office (GPAI).
regulation.penalties: Up to €35M or 7% of global annual turnover for prohibited-practice violations; lower tiers for other breaches.
regulation.covered_entities: Providers, deployers, importers, and distributors of AI systems placed on or used in the EU market, wherever established.
regulation.risk_classification: Risk-based: prohibited / high-risk / limited-risk transparency / minimal risk; separate GPAI model obligations.
regulation.applicability_notes: Phased: prohibitions + AI literacy from Feb 2, 2025; GPAI obligations from Aug 2, 2025; most high-risk obligations from Aug 2, 2026. Verify current milestones against EUR-Lex and the AI Office.

events.summary: Entered into force (application phased over 6-36 months).
Prohibited-practices provisions and AI literacy obligations became applicable.
General-purpose AI model obligations became applicable; governance rules operational.

name: NYC Local Law 144
description: Regulates automated employment decision tools (AEDTs): annual independent bias audits, public posting of audit results, and candidate notice requirements.

regulation.enforcement_authority: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP)
regulation.penalties: Civil penalties per violation per day; separate violations for audit, posting, and notice failures.
regulation.covered_entities: Employers and employment agencies using AEDTs for candidates/employees in New York City.
regulation.risk_classification: Automated employment decision tools (hiring and promotion).
regulation.applicability_notes: Enforcement began July 5, 2023 after DCWP final rules. Verify current guidance on the DCWP page.

events.summary: Local Law 144 took effect.
DCWP began enforcement following final rulemaking.

name: Utah AI Policy Act
description: SB 149 (2024): consumer-protection disclosure obligations for generative AI, plus an AI 'learning laboratory' program under the Office of AI Policy.

regulation.enforcement_authority: Utah Division of Consumer Protection; Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy
regulation.penalties: Administrative fines and enforcement under Utah consumer-protection law.
regulation.covered_entities: Entities using generative AI in regulated consumer interactions in Utah.
regulation.applicability_notes: Amended in subsequent sessions (scope refinements in 2025). Verify current text via the Utah Legislature site.

events.summary: AI Policy Act took effect — one of the first US state AI consumer-disclosure laws.

name: California SB 53 (Transparency in Frontier AI Act)
description: Requires large frontier AI developers to publish safety frameworks, report critical safety incidents, and provides whistleblower protections.

regulation.penalties: Civil penalties for noncompliance with disclosure and reporting obligations.
regulation.covered_entities: Large frontier AI model developers meeting compute/revenue thresholds.
regulation.risk_classification: Frontier model safety transparency and incident reporting.
regulation.applicability_notes: Companion to California's broader 2024-2025 AI legislative package (incl. AB 2013 training-data transparency). Verify thresholds and current amendments against the official bill text.

events.summary: Signed by Governor Newsom — first US frontier-model transparency law.
Operative date reached.

name: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act
description: HB 149 (2025): prohibits certain AI uses (behavioral manipulation, social scoring, certain biometric identification), sets government AI disclosure duties, creates a regulatory sandbox.

regulation.penalties: Civil penalties; cure period provisions for violations.
regulation.covered_entities: Developers and deployers of AI systems in Texas; specific government-agency obligations.
regulation.applicability_notes: Verify scope details against the enrolled bill text; several provisions were narrowed during passage.

events.summary: Signed by Governor Abbott.
TRAIGA took effect.

name: Illinois HB 3773 (AI in Employment)
description: Amends the Illinois Human Rights Act: employers may not use AI that discriminates in employment decisions and must give notice when AI is used for them.

regulation.penalties: Remedies under the Illinois Human Rights Act.
regulation.covered_entities: Employers using AI in recruitment, hiring, promotion, discipline, discharge, and related decisions affecting Illinois employees.
regulation.risk_classification: Employment discrimination via AI; notice obligations.

events.summary: AI employment-discrimination amendments took effect.

name: NIST AI RMF
description: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 — voluntary framework for managing AI risks across the lifecycle: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage.

events.summary: AI RMF 1.0 published.

name: NIST AI RMF Generative AI Profile
description: NIST AI 600-1 — cross-sectoral profile of the AI RMF for generative AI: 12 GAI risk categories and ~200 suggested actions.

events.summary: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) published alongside companion GenAI guidance.

name: ISO/IEC 42001
description: AI management system standard (AIMS) — requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an AI management system. Certifiable.

events.summary: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 published (December 2023) — first certifiable AI management system standard.

name: ISO/IEC 23894
description: AI — Guidance on risk management. Aligns AI risk management with ISO 31000 principles.

name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
description: OWASP GenAI Security Project's Top 10 risks for LLM applications — prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure, supply chain, excessive agency, and more.

events.summary: 2025 edition released (November 2024): unbounded consumption, vector/embedding weaknesses, system prompt leakage added.

name: OWASP Agentic AI Security
description: OWASP GenAI Security Project agentic AI workstream — threats and mitigations for autonomous/agentic AI systems.

events.summary: Agentic AI — Threats and Mitigations guidance published (February 2025).

name: MITRE ATLAS
description: Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems — knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques against AI, modeled after ATT&CK.

name: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework
description: IMDA/AI Verify Foundation framework for responsible AI deployment, including the Generative AI edition (May 2024) covering nine governance dimensions.
